backlog.spec: In _solve_once, unguided starts currently use a constant INIT_RADIUS=0.05. Instead draw the initial radii as rng.uniform(0.02, 0.12, n). Also start guided restarts from the incumbent's radii rather than 0.05 (multiply them by 0.95 so the start is near-feasible). Varied starting radii help SLSQP find mixed-size packings, which is where the optimum lies.
backlog.title: Randomized heterogeneous initial radii

backlog.spec: For non-guided restarts, with probability 0.5 draw the initial centres from a Gaussian mixture instead of the uniform box: pick k = rng.integers(2, 5) cluster means uniformly in [0.2, 0.8]^2, assign each circle to a random cluster, and add rng.normal(0, 0.12) noise to its mean, then clip to [0, 1]. The other half keeps the uniform start. Everything else (SLSQP, repair, time loop) is unchanged.
backlog.title: Clustered Gaussian-mixture starts

backlog.spec: Use fewer cheap restarts (MAX_ITER=100) then spend the last 25 percent of time re-running SLSQP from the best solution with maxiter=500 and tiny jitter (sd 1e-3), accepting only if the repaired sum improves. This gets full convergence on the best basin.
backlog.title: Raise MAX_ITER and polish best

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative repair with a vectorized one: clip radii to wall distances, then for all overlapping pairs scale down repeatedly until none remain, and use SHRINK=1e-12 plus a final check that the minimum slack >= -1e-12. Reduces the loss from shrinking, and the packing stays valid under the 1e-10 tolerance.
backlog.title: Tighter, exact repair

backlog.spec: After a first phase of random restarts (about 30 percent of time), switch to perturbation moves of the best: move 1-3 random circles to random positions (or swap two circles of different radii), plus jitter sd 0.01 on all, then re-optimize with SLSQP; accept if better. Replaces the current guided sd 0.03 global noise.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best with local perturbations

backlog.spec: Add a second guided move, used on half of the guided restarts. Take the best packing and pick two circles whose radii differ by more than 0.02. Swap their centres, keep their radii attached to their new positions, and scale both radii down by 0.9. Use the full centres+radii vector as x0 for SLSQP, with no other jitter. This explores how sizes are assigned to sites, which plain positional jitter rarely changes.
backlog.title: Swap-move perturbation

backlog.spec: Replace pure random restarts with basin hopping: after the first SLSQP run, repeatedly perturb the best packing (jitter centres by N(0, 0.02-0.05), occasionally relocate the smallest circle to a random free spot), re-run SLSQP from the perturbed point, and accept the new packing if its radius sum improves. Keep the time-limit loop and the final _repair call unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-start with basin hopping from best packing

backlog.spec: Add an init generator used with probability 0.5 for unguided restarts. Pick a random row pattern summing to 32 from a small list, e.g. [6,5,6,5,6,4], [5,6,5,6,5,5], [6,6,5,5,5,5], [4,5,6,6,5,6], [7,6,6,7,6]. Place the rows evenly in y over [0.1,0.9] and space the circles evenly in x within each row. Add N(0,0.02) jitter and shuffle. Set the initial radii from the row spacing: 0.5*min(dx, dy)*0.9. Feed this to SLSQP instead of the uniform-random base. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged.
backlog.title: Structured row-based initial layouts

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres with a jittered grid of points: choose a random rows/columns split for roughly n points, place centres on a staggered lattice with random spacing jitter, scale into [0.1, 0.9]^2, and randomly drop surplus points. This starts SLSQP from configurations closer to good dense packings than uniform random points do, while keeping the randomness seeded.
backlog.title: Biased random initialisation toward hexagonal-like layouts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after a short first SLSQP (maxiter 30) with all pairs, find the pairs with d_ij - r_i - r_j < 0.1. Re-run SLSQP with maxiter 200, keeping only those pair constraints plus the walls and r>=0, starting from the first result. About 100 pairs remain instead of 496, so each iteration is much cheaper. The existing repair pass ensures that any violation from a dropped pair is fixed.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: Split the time budget into an exploration phase (first 40 percent of TIME_FRACTION * time_limit, uniform random restarts) and a refinement phase (remaining time, guided restarts from the current best with a decreasing jitter scale from 0.05 down to 0.005). Make the jitter scale a linear function of elapsed fraction of time so refinement becomes progressively more local.
backlog.title: Adaptive time allocation between exploration and refinement

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the constant starting radius INIT_RADIUS with per-circle starting radii taken from the initial centres: r_i = min(0.5 * min_{j != i} |c_i - c_j|, c_i_x, c_i_y, 1 - c_i_x, 1 - c_i_y), floored at 1e-3. Compute these from the random initial centres before building x0 and keep the rest unchanged. The starting point is then closer to feasible for the pairwise constraints, which may change which basins SLSQP reaches.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour gap radius initialisation

backlog.spec: In solve(), change the guided-restart condition so guided restarts begin after 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit (instead of 0.5) and use probability 0.7 instead of 0.5. Keep everything else unchanged. This tunes the one change that helped (slot 1).
backlog.title: Guided fraction 0.7 from 30% of budget

backlog.spec: Keep a variable sigma in solve, starting at 0.03, and pass it to _solve_once as the jitter sd for guided restarts, in place of the hard-coded 0.03. After each guided restart: if the repaired result beats the best sum by more than 1e-7, multiply sigma by 1.5. Otherwise multiply it by 1.5**(-0.25). Clamp sigma to [0.004, 0.08]. Non-guided restarts do not change sigma.
backlog.title: 1/5 success rule for the guided jitter scale

backlog.spec: Start each restart with INIT_RADIUS drawn randomly in [0.03, 0.1], and first solve with a cheap penalty or equal-radius max-min problem is not needed; just randomize INIT_RADIUS per restart for diversity of local optima.
backlog.title: Smaller radius init with growth stage

backlog.spec: The guided restart jitter is fixed at sigma 0.03. Make it adaptive: keep a variable sigma that starts at 0.05. After each guided restart, multiply sigma by 0.8 if it improved the best sum by more than 1e-6. Otherwise multiply it by 1.1. Clamp sigma to [0.005, 0.1]. Also pass the best radii times 0.9 as the starting radii instead of INIT_RADIUS.
backlog.title: Adaptive jitter scale for guided restarts

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct solutions. After 40% of time, each restart picks a random elite and perturbs it with sd drawn from {0.005, 0.015, 0.03}, or reflects/rotates it by a random symmetry of the square first. Replace the worst elite if better and different (sum differs by >1e-6).
backlog.title: Elite pool restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the overlap-shrinking _repair with a greedy post-optimisation: after the boundary clamp, iterate over circles in random order and grow each radius to the maximum value allowed by the boundary and its current nearest neighbours (r_i = min(boundary slack, min over j of d_ij - r_j)), repeating a few passes. Only the shrink step at the end is still needed for numerical safety with a SHRINK of 1e-9. This recovers radius sum lost to the crude repair.
backlog.title: Smarter repair: greedy radius growth instead of shrinking

backlog.spec: Change the guided step in solve. Do not jitter every centre with N(0,0.03). Instead take the best packing and pick 1 to 3 circles, chosen with a bias toward small radii (probability proportional to 1/r). Move each to a uniform random point in the square with radius 0.01. Leave all other centres and radii at their best values and use the full vector (centres and radii) as x0. Then run SLSQP. Start guided restarts once a best exists after 30% of the time instead of 50%, and use them with probability 0.7.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep the guided restarts unchanged. For non-guided restarts, replace the uniform random centres with a jittered grid: a 6x6 grid of cell centres over [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2. Use the seed rng to choose n=32 of the 36 cells at random without replacement. Add uniform jitter of plus or minus 0.4 times the cell width to each centre, then clip to [0, 1]. Everything else stays as it is. This repeats slot 6 (-2.9386 without slot 1) on top of the current incumbent.
backlog.title: Stack jittered-grid starts on the guided incumbent

backlog.spec: In solve, when comparing a new repaired packing with the incumbent, treat it as better if its radius sum exceeds the incumbent's by more than 1e-4, or if the sums are within 1e-4 and the new packing has more circles touching a wall (|c - edge| <= r + 1e-9 on any side) than the incumbent. Keep the sum-based rule otherwise. This changes only which of near-equal packings is kept as incumbent, and so affects the guided restarts that start from it.
backlog.title: Wall-contact tie-break for restart selection

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92, and make the loop skip starting a new restart if the average restart duration would exceed the remaining time. Limit is 30 s CPU, so the margin is safe.
backlog.title: Use full time fraction

backlog.spec: In _repair, when a pair (i, j) overlaps by over = r_i + r_j - d_ij > 0, reduce only the smaller of the two radii, by exactly over (the smaller radius becomes max(smaller - over, 0)), instead of scaling both by d/(r_i+r_j). Keep the argmax selection and the wall clipping unchanged. Because the larger circle keeps its radius, the total loss from repair may be smaller on packings where one circle is much bigger than its neighbour.
backlog.title: Shrink-the-smaller-circle repair rule

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when init is None, place the first four centres at (INIT_LOW, INIT_LOW), (1-INIT_LOW, INIT_LOW), (INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW) and (1-INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW) with a small rng.normal(0, 0.01) jitter, and draw the remaining n-4 centres uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 as before. Keep the rest of the SLSQP solve and repair unchanged. This only changes the starting configuration, so it adds no new code paths beyond the initialisation line.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored random starts

backlog.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the constraint vector cons with respect to (centres, radii), built with numpy from the pair index arrays iu. Analytic Jacobians make each SLSQP iteration far cheaper for n=32, so more restarts and more iterations fit in the 24 s budget. Keep the constraint ordering and the objective unchanged.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep the guided restarts unchanged. With probability 0.5, a non-guided restart becomes a radius-continuation restart. Bisect a common radius R in [0.05, 0.12] for 6 steps. At each step, run a short SLSQP (maxiter=60) with the radii fixed at R that minimises the sum of squared overlaps, both pair overlaps and wall overlaps, over the centres. Warm-start each step from the previous step's centres. Keep the largest R that reaches near-zero overlap (below 1e-8). Then run the existing free-radius SLSQP from those centres, with radii R. This repeats slot 17 (-2.9380 without slot 1) on top of the current incumbent.
backlog.title: Stack radius-continuation restarts on the guided incumbent

backlog.spec: In the restart loop, after each SLSQP solve take the incumbent best, remove the circle with the smallest radius, and reinsert it at the point in a grid of candidate locations (e.g. 40x40 over [0,1]^2) that maximises the distance to the nearest centre minus its neighbours' radii. Re-run SLSQP from this configuration and keep it if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove smallest circle and reinsert

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, pass the box limits through minimize's bounds argument instead of as inequality constraints. Set bounds to (0, 1) for every centre coordinate and (0, 0.5) for every radius, and remove the r >= 0 entries from cons so that only the pairwise and wall-distance constraints remain. Wall constraints c - r >= 0 and 1 - c - r >= 0 stay as inequalities. The solver then receives the simple box limits natively, which can change convergence on the same starts.
backlog.title: Native SLSQP bounds for the box constraints

backlog.spec: For guided restarts, apply a random element of the dihedral group D4 of the unit square to the incumbent centres before jitter (random flip of x -> 1-x, y -> 1-y, and optional swap of x and y). The radii init stays constant. This diversifies the guided starts without changing the geometry of the packing.
backlog.title: Square-symmetry transform for guided starts

memo: Helped: only slot 1 (guided restarts in the second half, half start from the best packing), -2.9365, delta -0.0112. It is a single run and noise sd is about 0.0034, so it is unconfirmed. Not helped: nearly everything else, mostly within noise. That covers new initialisations (2, 9, 18, 29, 34), crossover (3), penalty or barrier solvers (4, 24), analytic gradients (5), gravity (10), pair pruning (11), successive halving (19), population/Metropolis schemes (20, 23), and post-polish steps (16, 28, 31, 33). Near misses, run without slot 1: 21 (-2.9396), 27 (-2.9396), 6 (-2.9386), 17 (-2.9380). Next: 1) replicate slot 1 to fix the baseline. 2) Tune the guided fraction and start time. 3) Stack slots 21/27 (the two best, same idea), then 6 and 17, one at a time on top of slot 1. 4) Final polish. Avoid more initialisation or post-polish ideas.
